text:
maya: Heads up — we saw a weird scaling loop on gpu-inference in eu-west-1 this morning. HPA fired on the external metric `inference_latency_95`, CA spun up 4 n1-preemptible-gpu nodes, pods scheduled, but within ~3m VPA recommended downsizing and HPA pulled back, CA started scale-down and then scale-up again. Net result: warm-pool starvation and tail latency spike. anyone seen this pattern before? :confused:

sam: ugh. timeline? any logs from CA or HPA? :eyes:

maya: timeline in a nutshell: request burst at 06:12 -> external metric spiked, HPA target=80% -> scaled replicas 3->12 -> CA detected pending pods and added 4 gpu nodes at 06:15 -> by 06:18 VPA recommendation applied (we have VPA in recommendation-only mode but a cron job applies it to keep pods small) -> pods got smaller, HPA target util hit lower -> replicas dropped 12->4 -> CA scale-down candidates at 06:22 -> warm pool exhausted -> new requests at 06:25 -> coldstart at pod level, latency jump.

jin: that sounds like a classic inertia mismatch between HPA/VPA and CA. The external metric is noisy and has short TTL. Are we using smoothing? current prometheus query is: `histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket[1m])) by (le))` which is pretty bursty.

maya: yes exactly — adapter exposes it as `external.googleapis.com/inference_latency_95` via prometheus-adapter. No smoothing and HPA interval is 30s.

sam: quick wins: increase HPA stabilizationWindowSeconds, add `behavior` with `scaleDown.stabilizationWindowSeconds: 300`, and bump `minReplicas` for gpu pool to avoid total collapse. Also tune CA: `--scale-down-unneeded-time=10m` and `--scale-down-delay-after-add=15m`.

leo: also consider using a movingAverage rule in the adapter for the metric so spikes don't immediately drive replica counts. Ex: `avg_over_time(inference_latency_95[3m])` in the expose rule.

maya: can someone paste example HPA snippet? I don't want to misconfigure.

sam: sure — example we tested in staging:

```yaml
apiVersion: autoscaling/v2
kind: HorizontalPodAutoscaler
metadata:
  name: gpu-inference-hpa
spec:
  scaleTargetRef:
    apiVersion: apps/v1
    kind: Deployment
    name: gpu-inference
  minReplicas: 3
  maxReplicas: 20
  metrics:
  - type: External
    external:
      metric:
        name: inference_latency_95
      target:
        type: AverageValue
        averageValue: "200ms"
  behavior:
    scaleDown:
      stabilizationWindowSeconds: 300
      policies:
      - type: Percent
        value: 30
        periodSeconds: 60
```

jin: that looks good. Also, consider making the HPA use `AverageValue` over a smoothed metric instead of instantaneous.

rk: infra-bot just posted CA events around that time: `cluster-autoscaler: scale-up: triggered by pending pods; 4 nodes added (preemptible)` and `cluster-autoscaler: scale-down: candidates found but delay active`. attaching snippet below — it shows the scale-down delay tightened by a custom flag change we rolled last week:

```
I0318 06:21:50 remote_autoscaler.go:203] Scale-down candidates: [node-gpu-7 node-gpu-9] total 2
I0318 06:22:10 leaderelection.go:110] waiting for 00:00:30 to pass before scaling down
```

leo: ah, we did lower `--scale-down-unneeded-time` last week to save cost. That explains the faster teardown. We traded cost for stability and hit this exact pattern. We should revert for gpu nodepools, or have different CA config per nodepool.

maya: yeah, per-nodepool flags would help. Right now CA is global. Any way to isolate?

sam: we can run dedicated CA for gpu nodepool(s) as a separate deployment with nodeSelector on cloud provider nodepools. That gives different flags and scale-down settings. It isn't trivial but has been done at other orgs.

jin: alternative: mark gpu nodes with high `ScaleDownExclusion` taint during provisioning window so CA won't remove them for X minutes. Or ensure k8s Warm Pool is populated. Cloud warm pool for GPUs is tricky though (images + driver init).

maya: warm pool idea: current warm pool size was 0 after 06:30. We don't have GPU warm snapshots; driver install takes ~90s. So it's not just CA delay, it's node init time.

rk: cost note: preemptibles are cheaper but create more churn. moving to reserved GPUs for a small baseline pool (2-4 nodes) might reduce tail latency at modest cost. We should show numbers: baseline 3 preemptible nodes cost ~ $0.4/hr, reserved 3 nodes ~$1.8/hr but reduces coldstarts.

leo: ops proposal: (1) revert aggressive scale-down flag for gpu CA, (2) deploy dedicated CA for gpu nodepool with `--scale-down-unneeded-time=20m`, `--max-empty-bulk-delete=0`, (3) add HPA stabilization and metric smoothing, (4) create a small reserved baseline pool of 2 nodes.

maya: sounds good. i'll open a short RFC with perf/cost sims. can someone volunteer to test HPA behavior in staging with smoothed metric? :hand:

sam: I can run the staging test today, will push adjusted prometheus-adapter rule and HPA behavior.

jin: i'll draft the adapter rule and a recording rule for `inference_latency_95_smoothed` using `avg_over_time(...[5m])` and push to staging alerting rules.

rk: i'll run cost calc and estimate monthly delta.

infra-bot: Deployment gpu-inference-hpa-v2 rolled out to staging by sam at 2026-03-18T10:20:00Z. :rocket:

maya: thanks all. let's sync tomorrow after staging tests. :thumbsup:
